case_name: Zahoor and Others v State of Uttar Pradesh
respondent:
State of Uttar Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

25 October 1990
Cr.A. No. 587 of 1979 (From the Judgment and Order Dt. 28 April 1978 of the Allahabad High Court in Cr.A. No. 265 of 1973)
The Judgment was delivered by: K. Jayachandra Reddy, J.
1. There are three appellants in this appeal and they figured as accused 1, 11 and 12 before the trial court. They along with nine other accused 2 to 10 were tried for offences punishable u/s. 302 read with Section 149, S. 325 read with Section 149, S. 323 read with Ss. 149 and 452 IPC. The trial court acquitted all the 12 accused. facts: The case involves three appellants who were tried for offences punishable under sections 302, 325, and 323 IPC.
The trial court acquitted all the 12 accused.

The State of U.P. preferred an appeal against the said order of acquittal and the High Court convicted the three appellants u/s. 302 read with S. 149 IPC and sentenced each of them to undergo imprisonment for life, under S. 323 read with S. 149 to undergo one year's RI, under S. 325 read with S. 149 to undergo five years' RI and u/s. 148 to further undergo 2 years' RI.
The deceased, Idris, was a well-to-do man of the village and his house was situated in the midst of the village.
About a week prior to the occurrence the deceased had purchased the tobacco field of the Ghulam Lodh and paid Rs. 300 as earnest money.
Ghulam Lodh, however, sold that plot subsequently to accused 1 and 9.
The miscreants assaulted the labourers in the courtyard.
Thereafter all those who were outside his house, also entered the inner courtyard.
On seeing them the deceased, his son and his two brothers ran to take shelter in the western kothri and closed the door.
Some of the labourers including PW 2 however, stayed in the inner courtyard.
issues: Whether the FIR was lodged belatedly after due deliberations?
Whether the witnesses were all interested and their evidence ought not to have been relied upon by the High Court?

Whether the defence version namely that some unknown assailants committed dacoity in the house of the deceased on that night and caused the death of the deceased and also caused injuries to PWs, is probable?
petitioner_arguments: The FIR was lodged belatedly after due deliberations.
The witnesses were all interested and their evidence ought not to have been relied upon by the High Court.
The defence version namely that some unknown assailants committed dacoity in the house of the deceased on that night and caused the death of the deceased and also caused injuries to PWs, is probable.
respondent_arguments: There was no inordinate delay in giving the earliest report.

All the material particulars are mentioned and coming to the attack on the deceased it is clearly stated that accused 1 put bricks underneath the neck of the fallen deceased and then a lathi was kept on the throat and pressed from one end by accused 1 and 12 and from the other end by accused 9 and Adharey resulting in the death of the deceased.
court_reasoning: The evidence of PWs 2 and 4 was rejected on the ground that the former was an employee of the deceased and later was a permanent labourer.

The learned Sessions Judge observed that the evidence of the eye-witnesses was not consistent in naming the culprits in the statements made in the course of the investigation and in the evidence during the trial.
The High Court, on the other hand, held that the specific overt acts of the three appellants and two others Gajju and Adharey were established but Gajju died during the pendency of the appeal.
holding: The High Court convicted the three appellants u/s. 302 read with S. 149 IPC and sentenced each of them to undergo imprisonment for life, under S. 323 read with S. 149 to undergo one year's RI, under S. 325 read with S. 149 to undergo five years' RI and u/s. 148 to further undergo 2 years' RI.
